children: Augmont Enterprises shares fell more than 3.5 percent from their listing price on Monday after making a strong debut earlier in the day, with analysts recommending partial profit booking and a stop-loss of Rs 900.
The shares of the company hit an intraday low of Rs 927 per share on the NSE, down 3.54 percent from the listing price of Rs 961 per share.
The stock, however, remained up 17.64 percent over its IPO price of Rs 788 per share.

Shivani Nyati, Head of Wealth at Swastika Investmart, said the company's high revenue is largely driven by bullion trading volumes, while its PAT margin remains below 0.4 percent, leaving limited room for margin expansion.

"Moreover, promoter-group entity Riddisiddhi Bullions contributed around 27.44 percent of FY26 revenue, while the top 10 customers accounted for 52.09 percent, with no long-term contracts, highlighting concentration and governance risks," she said.
"At the IPO price, valuations were already relatively rich at around 18.5-19.5x FY26 P/E and 6.8-7.1x P/B, making the post-listing premium less attractive for fresh buying," Nyati said.

"For allotted investors, we suggest to book partial profits and hold the half with a stop-loss of Rs 900. A sustained move above Rs 1,000 could support further upside, whereas a break below Rs 900 would warrant caution," she added.
Augmont Enterprises shares made a decent market debut at nearly 22 percent above their IPO price, following a 105.78-times subscription to its issue in the primary market between August 21 and 25.
Shares of Augmont Enterprises were listed at Rs 961 per share on the NSE, a premium of 21.95 percent. The Rs 825-crore issue had a price band of Rs 750-788 per share.
On the BSE, the shares of the integrated gold and silver platform company were listed at Rs 956 per share, a premium of 21.32 percent.
